question: The device or programme that enables a computer to transmit data over telephones and cable lines is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**modem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A modem (short for modulator-demodulator) is a device that converts digital data from a computer into an analog signal that can be transmitted over telephone or cable lines and vice versa.
 
• It modulates an analog carrier signal to encode digital information, and also demodulates the carrier signal to decode the transmitted information.
 
• Modems are used for various types of data transfer, including Internet access, email, and file transfers.
 
• They come in different types, such as dial-up modems, DSL modems, and cable modems, each suited for specific types of connections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Motherboard:**

 
 
• The motherboard is the main printed circuit board (PCB) in a computer that holds the CPU, memory, and other essential components.
 
• It provides connectors for other peripherals.
 
• Motherboards come in different sizes and form factors, such as ATX, MicroATX, and Mini-ITX.
 
• It is crucial for ensuring all components of the computer can communicate with each other.
 
 
 
• **Monitor:**
 
 
• A monitor is an output device that displays information in pictorial form.
 
• It usually consists of a screen, circuitry, a power supply, and buttons to adjust settings.
 
• Monitors can be CRT, LCD, or LED, with varying resolutions and sizes.
 
• They are essential for users to interact with the computer's graphical interface.
 
 
 
• **Mouse:**
 
 
• A mouse is a hand-held pointing device that detects two-dimensional motion relative to a surface.
 
• This motion is typically translated into the motion of a pointer on a display.
 
• There are different types of mice, such as optical and laser mice, which use light to detect movement.
 
• Mice are crucial for navigation and interaction with the computer's user interface.
